title: Why do cats purr?
hook: Hi friends! Have you heard a cat make a soft rumbly sound? Why do cats purr?
answer: Inside a cat's throat are tiny stretchy strings. When a cat breathes in and out, it wiggles those strings super fast, like a little drum that never stops. That wiggle makes the gentle rumble we call purring. Cats purr when they feel cosy and safe, like you under a warm blanket.
wowFact: Here is a wow fact! Kittens start purring when they are only a few days old, before their eyes even open. The purr helps their mum find them.
experiment: Try this! Put your hand on your neck and hum a long, low sound. Can you feel a tiny buzz under your fingers? That is a bit like a purr!

onScreenText.answer: A tiny wiggle in the throat
onScreenText.wowFact: Kittens purr before they can see
onScreenText.experiment: Try it: hum and feel the buzz

description: Bolt finds out why cats purr and what the soft rumble means. Then he tries a gentle humming experiment to feel a purr in his own throat.
